eips.title: State Creation Gas Cost Increase
eips.summary: Central topic of the call: impact on deployed contracts, broken invariants, audit findings, and whether to proceed with Glamsterdam.

moments.context: Danceratopz introduced EIP-8037 and EIP-8038 as proposed Glamsterdam changes that were found to break smart contract invariants late in development.
Marius explained that 8037 and 8038 were proposed in 2025 to enable 3.3-3.5x scaling of Ethereum, significantly reducing costs for most users.
ChainSecurity presented their audit findings, reporting 152 findings from on-chain and off-chain analysis of contracts affected by 8037 and 8038 changes.
Dedaub presented their independent impact study on EIP-8037 and 8038, finding 12 high and 70 medium confirmed findings via decompiled contract analysis and transaction replays.
Jango from Juicebox described how 8037 breaks try/catch composability, allowing users to tune gas to skip composable elements, undermining protocol safety.
Marius argued the affected contracts are a fringe subset of approximately 10-15K out of 90 million, and benefits outweigh the drawbacks.
Mario from the specs team said EIP-8037 left a mark and they will now review every specification change through the lens of the application layer.
Danceratopz said removing 8037 would cause a serious delay to Glamsterdam, potentially half a year, and it is important for sustainable state growth.
Daniel from Uniswap urged that 8037's gas reservoir handling should be reconsidered because it fundamentally breaks try/catch and introduces implicit branching based on user-set gas.
Toni explained that EIP-7825's transaction gas limit cap in the prior fork made 8037 necessary even to deploy max-size contracts, and removing it would reintroduce that limitation.

eips.title: State-Access Gas Cost Update
eips.summary: Discussed alongside EIP-8037 as part of the Glamsterdam gas repricing changes that break contract invariants.

moments.context: Danceratopz introduced EIP-8038 together with EIP-8037 as the Glamsterdam changes found to break smart contract invariants.
Marius said 8037 and 8038 together enable significant scaling and cost reductions but break invariants that contracts relied on.
ChainSecurity's audit covered both 8037 and 8038, finding most breakages came from gas cost increases rather than the new reservoir mechanism.
Dedaub presented their impact study covering both EIP-8037 and 8038 changes to gas accounting and refund mechanisms.

eips.title: Revamped CALL instructions
eips.summary: Potuz noted finding explicit mentions against gas schedule introspection in EIP-7069.

moments.context: Potuz asked why the gas schedule is not exposed in the EVM, saying he found explicit mentions against this in EIP-7069.

eips.title: Gas cost increases for state access opcodes
eips.summary: Cited as the precedent where core devs already accepted that a state-cost increase would break some deployed contracts.

moments.context: Marius said the core dev community made this call before — "with… 29, 30, with the increase in state access costs" — knowing some contracts would break, so the absolute-immutability assumption was broken much earlier.

eips.title: Transaction Gas Limit Cap
eips.summary: Cited as a prior fork's transaction gas limit cap that made EIP-8037 necessary for deploying large contracts.

moments.context: Toni explained that EIP-7825 in the last fork capped transaction gas, making 8037 necessary to even deploy max-size contracts under the new limit.

eips.summary: Ben Adams noted that moving refunds to end of transaction breaks ERC-4337 bundling and current account abstraction.

moments.context: Ben Adams said moving refund to end of transaction breaks 4337 bundling, causing issues for current account abstraction.

eips.title: REVERT instruction
eips.summary: Jochem referenced EIP-140 as the REVERT instruction spec when discussing subcall revert behavior.

moments.context: Jochem linked to EIP-140 when clarifying that REVERT puts 0 on the stack with reason in returndata, in context of subcall error handling.
